body_markdown:
Paying your global team members comes with a very clear problem:[hidden fees and opaque routing](https://srmcorp.com/understanding-the-hidden-costs-of-cross-border-payments-a-growing-business-risk/) delays. The World Bank's[Remittance Prices Worldwide report](https://remittanceprices.worldbank.org/sites/default/files/2026-04/RPW_main_report_and_annex_Q325.pdf) puts the global average cost of sending money across borders at 6.36% of the amount sent. At that rate, a $10,000 payout batch loses $636 to fees before a single payee is paid.


Our view: choose a cross border payments service built around the payee, with a payments API, real time payments rails, and tax forms under one contract. Skip corporate accounts built for spend, because they leave you to manage currency conversions and local compliance rules on your own.


**TLDR:**


- Pay global sellers and creators by connecting domestic networks to international rails.
- Resolve routing friction by handling currency conversion and regulatory compliance.
- Airwallex provides corporate cards, while Payoneer offers local receiving accounts.
- Dots bundles real-time rails via API to verify KYC and automate year-end 1099 filings.


## What Are Cross Border Payments Services


Cross border payments services allow businesses to send funds to recipients in different countries. This infrastructure connects domestic financial networks to international rails. It lets you[send money internationally](https://usedots.com/platform/international-payments/) to sellers, creators, or contractors globally. A[global payments API](https://usedots.com/platform/payouts-api/) bridges distinct banking architectures and localized payout methods, so you build one payment integration instead of one per country.


These[international payment methods](https://usedots.com/blog/the-best-global-payment-methods/) handle currency conversion and compliance across different regulatory environments. When you distribute funds internationally, you must manage fragmented infrastructure across multiple providers.


Stitching together separate tools for payee onboarding and fraud screening creates multi-week integration timelines. You also face high FX markups and rising overhead as your country count grows. A unified API resolves this friction by routing funds through local payment networks to settle in seconds, while[automated payouts](https://usedots.com/platform/payouts-automation/) remove the manual batch work.


## How We Ranked Cross Border Payments Services


Moving money internationally involves opaque routing and hidden fees. To give you a clear view of the market, we researched these cross border payments providers based on how well they resolve routing friction. Our ranking relies entirely on each provider's pricing pages, API docs, and help-center articles. We weighted the mechanics that govern how fast payees receive their funds, including wire vs ACH routing choices.


Our ranking criteria include the following metrics:


- Geographic reach. We checked if the provider supports disbursements across[190+ countries](https://usedots.com/platform/coverage-map) using local payment networks.
- Settlement speed. We looked for systems that route funds through real-time rails to settle in seconds without instant payout surcharges.
- Automated compliance. We checked whether the service verifies payee identity and files tax forms automatically.

## Airwallex


Airwallex provides global payment infrastructure with multi-currency accounts, spend management tools, and support for regional rails such as Unified Payments Interface. For international business transfers, the company focuses on corporate card features for foreign spending.


### What They Offer


- Multi-currency business accounts for holding and routing international funds securely.
- Payment gateway integration to accept foreign currencies directly at customer checkout.


A team with a European vendor base can hold euros, British pounds, and US dollars in separate wallets, then pay invoices in the recipient's local currency without a forced conversion step. The corporate card issues virtual and physical versions, so a finance lead can set per-employee spend limits for travel or ad spend in a foreign market. Expense data syncs to common accounting tools, which cuts the manual reconciliation work tied to reimbursing staff who travel across borders.


The checkout integration supports card payments, local wallets, and bank transfers across dozens of markets, so an online store can present a shopper in Singapore with Singapore dollar pricing at checkout. Settlement into the business account typically follows standard banking timelines rather than the instant rails built for payouts. Teams running both customer checkout and contractor payouts often pair this toolset with a payouts-specific provider to keep the two workflows separate.


### Evaluation


- Good for: Airwallex allows teams to hold foreign balances and issue cards for international travel and vendor purchases.
- Limitations: Routing external contractor payments through this infrastructure often relies on traditional banking rails that take several days to clear.
- Bottom line: Rely on Airwallex for internal employee expenses, but integrate Dots to settle high-volume payee disbursements in seconds.


## Payoneer


Payoneer operates a money transfer service aimed at online sellers and independent businesses. Moving capital internationally requires dedicated financial infrastructure. While Payoneer maintains a strong presence in the e-commerce sector, many teams look for[Payoneer alternatives](https://usedots.com/alternatives/payoneer/) , and we built Dots to provide automated compliance and payout flexibility through a single API.


### What They Offer


- Local receiving accounts.
- Point of sale transaction capabilities.


**Limitation:** Routing payouts through Payoneer relies on standard banking networks, which results in multi-day settlement times instead of instant transfers.


A seller who earns from several marketplaces can receive USD, EUR, and GBP into local receiving accounts, then withdraw to a local bank account. That setup suits freelancers and online sellers who collect revenue from many buyers. The structure centers on the seller collecting money, not the business sending it.


Teams that pay out at volume need more than a place to receive funds. They need payee identity checks before funds move, tax-form collection, and one contract for every country. We built Dots to cover those steps through one API, so a business sending thousands of payouts a month does not add a separate vendor for each task.

## FAQ


### How should you choose between Dots, Airwallex, and Payoneer for international transfers?


Base your decision on your primary financial workflow. Use Airwallex for corporate spend management, Payoneer for standard e-commerce receiving accounts, and Dots if you need an API to route funds to global contractors instantly.


### Is Dots or Airwallex better for managing your corporate expenses abroad?


Airwallex is built for corporate expenses, offering multi-currency business accounts and corporate cards for foreign spending. Dots operates differently, focusing entirely on payout infrastructure that lets you pay sellers, creators, and contractors globally.


If your team books flights, pays for hotels, or covers vendor invoices while traveling abroad, Airwallex gives finance staff a card and a multi-currency balance to draw from directly. A marketing team running a trade show in Germany, for example, can hold euros in an Airwallex account and issue employee cards instead of relying on personal reimbursement. That setup works well for internal spend, but it was not built to onboard thousands of external payees, run KYC (Know Your Customer) checks, or generate tax forms at scale.


Dots solves a different problem: paying large numbers of sellers, creators, or contractors who are outside your company and need funds in local currency within seconds. A marketplace with 5,000 sellers in 40 countries, for instance, needs automated identity verification and 1099 (US tax form) generation, not a corporate card. Choose Airwallex for employee and vendor spend management, and choose Dots when your payout volume or payee count makes manual onboarding and compliance tracking impractical.


### How do services like Dots and Payoneer execute payee compliance for your business?


These providers adapt their compliance steps to fit their core users. Dots runs identity checks through[KYC (Know Your Customer) verifications](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/k/knowyourclient.asp) before funds move and generates 1099 filings at year-end. Payoneer uses localized receiving structures built for online sellers.


### Can you use Airwallex or Payoneer to pay your contractors as fast as Dots?


Airwallex and Payoneer move money across borders but often route funds through standard, multi-day banking networks. Dots bundles real time payments rails to settle funds immediately. You gain immediate settlement through the Dots payments API without paying extra instant-transfer fees.
